Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
153 AM EST Sat Nov 28 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The Gale Warning has been canceled.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Dry and breezy with seasonable temperatures today.

2) A frontal system will bring rain and gusty winds to the area 
Sunday night into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1... 
The area remains between departing low pressure to the north and 
high pressure to the south through tonight. The resulting pressure 
gradient will allow for another day of breezy conditions, with gusts 
of 25 to 30 mph. Went closer to the NBM90th to capture some higher 
gusts mixing down which lines up with RRFS and GFS model 
soundings. Otherwise, cyclonic flow aloft will keep plenty of 
clouds around, especially this morning into early afternoon.

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Attention then turns to a shortwave currently over the northwestern 
US. This shortwave will aid in development of a surface low that 
will track up from the Southern Plains tonight and pass to our north 
on Monday. This system will bring rain and gusty winds to the area 
Sunday night into Monday.

While a period of moderate rain is expected ahead of the cold 
front, this looks to be a quick moving system bringing a 
widespread 0.75 to 1.0 inches over a 6 to 12 hour period. At 
this time there are no hydrologic concerns. The latest RRFS 
model reflectivity shows a fine convective line moving through 
Long Island and CT Monday morning along the cold front. However,
both the RRFS and REFS model soundings show a very low and weak
CAPE profile. Lightning is not expected, but this may be 
something to watch for with the potential for some higher winds 
to mix down, as well as brief heavier rain.

There is a chance to meet marginal wind Advisory criteria. The 
better chance for this may actually be behind the system Monday 
afternoon with decent mixing. Winds will then gradually subside
Monday night.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
The terminals will remain between departing low pressure and high 
pressure to the south.

Mainly VFR overnight. Cigs should lower to MVFR during the daylight 
hours, and return to VFR tonight. Exceptions to this are KGON which 
should remain VFR, and KBDR which should have limited MVFR cigs in 
the afternoon. 

High confidence in WSW flow 10-15 kt with gusts 20-25 kt, though 
some outlying terminals should diminish to 10 kt with occasional 
gusts 15-20 kt overnight until around 13Z-14Z. 

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

Unscheduled amendments possible only if cigs lower to MVFR sooner 
than fcst. There is also the chance that cigs remain VFR for
most of the daylight hours.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Sunday through Wednesday... 

Late tonight: VFR with diminishing W flow. 

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night and Monday: Rain likely with MVFR or lower cond
after midnight through early Monday morning. Rain could persist
E of the NYC metro terminals after sunrise, but improving cond
likely through the day. S winds G20-30 kt late Sunday night with
a few hours of LLWS possible, then W winds G25-35 kt on Monday.
Winds diminish Monday night.

Tuesday and Wednesday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
The Gale warning has been canceled. Small Craft Advisories are
in effect for all waters through today and step down tonight as
winds lighten.

The next chance for SCA or Gales will be Sunday night through 
Monday night with a frontal system. The mention of gales remains
in the HWO. Southerly wind gusts up to 40 kt are possible late 
Sunday night into Monday morning and then gusts may remain up to
40 kt through Monday with a wind shift to the W/NW.

&&
